metadata.pr_description:
This PR address #17416 where it should be passed *args accordingly to logger

to format with `%s` instead of f-string

Signed-off-by: Aaron Pham <contact@aarnphm.xyz>

review_planner.summary: The provided diff includes changes across multiple files primarily related to logging improvements and minor string formatting updates.

tasks.title: Check for Injection Points
tasks.description: Review all uses of formatted strings in vllm/logger.py to ensure there are no injection vulnerabilities. Specifically, check `_print_info_once`, `_print_warning_once`, and methods in `_VllmLogger` class.

tasks.title: Check Logger Logic
tasks.description: Ensure that the logic in the logger functions (`_print_info_once`, `_print_warning_once`) and their usage in various files remains correct after the changes. Verify that the new argument handling does not introduce errors.

tasks.title: Assess Logger Performance Impact
tasks.description: Analyze the performance implications of the changes made to the logger functions (`_print_info_once`, `_print_warning_once`). Ensure that the introduction of variable arguments does not degrade performance unnecessarily.

tasks.title: Review Logger Consistency
tasks.description: Ensure that the changes to the logger functions (`_print_info_once`, `_print_warning_once`) and their usage across different files are consistent and adhere to best practices. Check for any inconsistencies in string formatting and argument usage.

worker_reports.context_summary: The review focuses on ensuring consistency and adherence to best practices for logger functions (`_print_info_once`, `_print_warning_once`) and their usage across various files. The primary issue identified is the transition from using f-string formatting to using `%` formatting in the logger messages, which is inconsistent with the updated definitions of `_print_info_once` and `_print_warning_once` functions that now accept variable arguments (`*args`).
warnings: No additional warnings were generated during the review.

worker_reports.context_summary: No critical issues were found in the provided code changes related to the logger functions and their usage. The changes primarily involve updating the logger calls to use formatted strings instead of f-strings, which is consistent and does not introduce any functional issues.
warnings: The changes are mostly stylistic and involve replacing f-strings with `%` formatting in logger calls. This is generally a good practice for consistency and potential performance benefits, but it does not affect the correctness of the logger functionality.

worker_reports.context_summary: No significant performance regressions or scalability risks were identified in the changes related to the logger functions `_print_info_once` and `_print_warning_once`. The introduction of variable arguments does not appear to introduce any unnecessary performance degradation based on the provided context.
warnings: The changes primarily involve updating string formatting to use `%` placeholders instead of f-strings in several logging statements. This change does not introduce any apparent performance issues, but it is worth noting that f-strings are generally more efficient than `%` formatting in Python 3.6 and later due to their inline evaluation and reduced overhead. However, the impact is likely negligible in the context of logging statements.

worker_reports.context_summary: No concrete security issues were found in the provided context. All formatted string usages in `vllm/logger.py` and related files have been reviewed, and no injection vulnerabilities were identified.
